source.stem:
Some children were asked to choose their favourite type of pet.
The pie chart shows the results.

parts.text: 41 children chose Cat. Work out how many children were asked altogether. [2]
Work out how many children chose Hamster. [2]

hinge.title: When interpreting a line graph, decide which conclusions are supported by points, peaks, lows, slopes, and intervals shown in the graph.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Trend is the label that belongs on this item, so 'When interpreting a line graph, decide which conclusions are supported' is answered as trend rather than inference.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: inference still holds here even though Compare slopes only over intervals shown on the graph and on the same vertical scale is missing from the stem — on the item about When interpreting a line graph, decide which.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Trend is what produces inference, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about When interpreting a line graph, decide which.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The inference rule also covers this: {'excluded_case': 'Do not infer a value for a country, person, or group not shown in the graph.', 'reason', so it is not an exception — on the item about When interpreting a line graph, decide which.

intelligence.enrichment: A supported interpretation of a line graph comes from the plotted values and how they change: peaks and lows identify high and low values, and steeper line segments show greater change over the same interval.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Mathematics question. Chapter: math/grade_08/ch_205. The student must decide: When interpreting a line graph, decide which conclusions are supported by points, peaks, lows, slopes, and intervals shown in the graph. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Supply exactly one complete tikzpicture. The stem must refer to that figure. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
